mainTopic: Blemishes that do and do not permit slaughtering a בכור: גרב and חזזית, old, sick and sin-related animals, and whether the אנדרוגינוס's female organ counts as a 'crack'.
overview: A ברייתא first explains that the 'joint' a calf's tail must reach is the upper joint, which is easy to see on a camel. A short משנה then says that all the listed blemishes let us slaughter a בכור and redeem פסולי המוקדשין. The גמרא explains that this line is a סתם ruling, so the הלכה follows even the blemishes taught by single תנאים. The next משנה lists conditions that are not real blemishes, and also discusses a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. The גמרא asks why גרב and חזזית are not blemishes when the Torah lists them, and it ends up splitting them into kinds that heal and kinds that never heal. It then finds פסוקים showing that old, sick, foul-smelling and sin-related animals cannot be brought as קרבנות. Last, it asks why an אנדרוגינוס is not slaughtered for the 'crack' of its female organ. אביי and רבא each prove that a crack in flesh is not a מום, and the גמרא explains how רבי ישמעאל disagrees with both.

steps.title: Which joint the calf's tail must reach
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the 'joint' in the calf's tail case is the upper joint, not the lower one, and that this joint is easy to see in a camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: the upper joint, not the lower joint. The matching joint in a camel can be seen clearly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain a word from the earlier משנה about a calf whose tail does not reach the joint (קפץ).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a calf's tail that does not reach the קפץ counts as a blemish, but a leg has more than one joint. The ברייתא tells us it means the upper joint. Since that joint is hard to see on a calf, it adds that on a camel the same joint stands out, which helps you picture where it is.

phrases.english: Gemara: It was taught:
The upper joint, and not the lower joint;
and the matching one in a camel is noticeable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: קֶפֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹן וְלֹא קֶפֶץ הַתַּחְתּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a term from the משנה before this point on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'joint' that the calf's tail must reach is the upper joint, whose match is clearly visible on a camel.

steps.title: These blemishes allow slaughtering and redeeming
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that for all the blemishes listed, a בכור may be slaughtered and פסולי המוקדשין may be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: For these blemishes we slaughter the firstborn, and disqualified consecrated animals are redeemed because of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה sums up the whole list of blemishes: they allow a בכור to be slaughtered and disqualified sacred animals to be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור with a lasting blemish cannot be offered, so it may be slaughtered and eaten outside the מקדש. An animal that was set aside as a קרבן and then got a blemish (פסולי המוקדשין) can be redeemed and become regular animal. The משנה says all the blemishes listed so far count for both.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn male animal, which is holy
Sacred animals that became unfit for the altar

phrases.english: Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: עַל אֵלּוּ מוּמִין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר,
phrases.english: For these blemishes one slaughters the firstborn,
and disqualified consecrated animals are redeemed on their account.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל אֵלּוּ מוּמִין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה closing the list of blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the listed blemishes allow a בכור to be slaughtered and allow פסולי המוקדשין to be redeemed.

steps.title: Why repeat what the start of the chapter said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה says this at all, since the beginning of the פרק already said a בכור is slaughtered for these blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this again? He already taught it in the first part: for these blemishes one slaughters the firstborn!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for repeating itself, because the opening line of the פרק said the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to say extra words. The פרק opened with 'על אלו מומין שוחטין את הבכור', so saying it again at the end looks unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this again?

phrases.english: Gemara: Why do I need this again?
He already taught it in the first part:
phrases.notes: The 'first part' is the opening line of this פרק.

phrases.aramaic: עַל אֵלּוּ מוּמִין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר!
phrases.english: For these blemishes one slaughters the firstborn!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה in step 2 for repeating itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first clause of the משנה in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same line already opens the פרק, so repeating it seems pointless.

steps.title: The second half, about redeeming, is the new part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה needed to teach the second half: that פסולי המוקדשין are redeemed for these blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last part was needed: disqualified consecrated animals are redeemed because of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the new teaching is the redeeming of disqualified sacred animals. The first half is only there to lead into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening of the פרק spoke only about a בכור. This answer says the משנה repeats the בכור line only to add that the same blemishes work for redeeming פסולי המוקדשין.

phrases.english: The last part was needed:
disqualified consecrated animals are redeemed on their account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a new detail in the second half of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole line seemed to repeat the opening of the פרק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The point of the line is the new rule about redeeming פסולי המוקדשין.

steps.title: Redeeming is obvious too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if these blemishes are strong enough to let us slaughter a בכור, of course they let us redeem פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is obvious. If we may slaughter, is redeeming even a question?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer by saying the 'new' part is not new at all, because it follows by simple logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering a בכור and eating it outside the מקדש is the bigger step. If a blemish is enough for that, it is surely enough for the smaller step of redeeming a disqualified sacred animal. So the second half also seems to teach nothing new.

phrases.english: This too is obvious —
if we may slaughter,
is redeeming even a question?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 4 as not giving any real new teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 4 that the redeeming clause is the new part.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a blemish allows the stronger step of slaughtering a בכור, it obviously allows the weaker step of redeeming.

steps.title: The unnamed ruling makes the halacha follow the individual views
steps.stepSummary: The real reason for the line: the משנה just brought views of single תנאים and said 'we have not heard these', so it repeats the rule without a name to show the הלכה follows all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since he taught 'he added three' and they said to him 'we have not heard these', and then he went on to teach the views of individuals, he states it without a name for all of them: for these blemishes one slaughters the firstborn, and disqualified consecrated animals are redeemed because of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. The line is not there to teach a new law. It is a סתם משנה placed after disputed and individual opinions, to tell us the הלכה follows all the listed blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the משנה said אילא added three blemishes and the חכמים answered 'we have not heard these'. Then it taught rulings from single תנאים. A reader might think those blemishes do not count in practice. By repeating the rule as a סתם משנה right after them, the משנה shows that the הלכה follows all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: We have not heard (we have no tradition of this)
States it without naming anyone (a סתם ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: The closing line of the משנה is not a new law. It is a סתם ruling that tells us the הלכה follows all the blemishes listed, including those taught by single תנאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a סתם משנה placed after individual views can decide the הלכה in their favor.

phrases.english: Rather, since he taught
'he added three,'
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier משנה where אִילָא added three blemishes.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: and they said to him: We have not heard these,
and he went on to teach the views of individuals,
so he states it without a name, covering all of them:

phrases.aramaic: עַל אֵלּוּ מוּמִין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר
phrases.english: For these blemishes one slaughters the firstborn
and disqualified consecrated animals are redeemed on their account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the answer of step 4, which step 5 knocked down, and answers the original question of step 3 in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the repeated line as a סתם ruling that decides the הלכה, not as a new law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line seemed to be a pointless repeat or an obvious addition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line comes after individual and disputed views to show that the הלכה follows all the listed blemishes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows all the blemishes in the פרק, including those taught by single תנאים, both for slaughtering a בכור and for redeeming פסולי המוקדשין.

steps.title: The list of blemishes that do not permit slaughtering a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists blemishes and conditions for which a בכור is not slaughtered, neither in the מקדש nor in the rest of the country.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the blemishes for which we do not slaughter a בכור, neither in the מקדש nor in the rest of the country. They are: pale spots on the eye; tears that are not constant; inner gums that were damaged but not pulled out; an animal with גרב, with warts, or with חזזית; an old animal, a sick animal, or one with a foul smell; an animal that was used for a sin; and an animal that killed a person, when the sin or the killing is known only from one witness or from the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It gives a list of problems that are not strong enough to count as real blemishes, so a בכור that has them may not be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משניות listed blemishes that do let us slaughter a בכור. This משנה gives the opposite list, problems that do not qualify. The last two cases, a sin done with the animal or an animal that killed a person, are included only when the fact rests on one witness or on the owner's word.

keyTerms.meaning: A pale or white spot on the eye
A type of boil or skin sore
A type of rash or boil

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
And these are the ones for which we do not slaughter
neither in the Temple nor in the country:
a pale spot, and tears that are not constant,
and inner gums that were damaged,
but not ones that were pulled out,
and one with boils, and one with warts,
and one with a rash, an old one, a sick one, and a foul-smelling one,
and one with which a sin was done,
and one that killed a person,

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד אוֹ עַל פִּי הַבְּעָלִים.
phrases.english: based on one witness or based on the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין עֲלֵיהֶן, לֹא בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ וְלֹא בַּמְּדִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The listed blemishes and conditions do not permit slaughtering a בכור, neither in the מקדש nor in the country.

steps.title: The dispute about a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are not slaughtered. רבי שמעון calls it the greatest blemish, and חכמים say an אנדרוגינוס is not a בכור at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are not slaughtered, neither in the מקדש nor in the country. רבי שמעון says: there is no blemish greater than this. חכמים say: it is not a בכור at all. Instead it may be sheared and used for work.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two more cases, an animal whose gender is hidden and an animal with both male and female organs, and brings three opinions about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion puts these animals on the list of animals that are not slaughtered. רבי שמעון disagrees: being a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס is itself the greatest blemish, so the animal may be slaughtered. חכמים go further and say an אנדרוגינוס has no בכור holiness at all, so it is treated like an ordinary animal that may be sheared and worked.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose sexual organs are covered over, so we cannot tell its gender
An animal with both male and female organs
It may be sheared and used for work, like an ordinary animal

phrases.english: And a tumtum and a hermaphrodite,
neither in the Temple nor in the country.
Rabbi Shimon says:
You have no blemish greater than this,
and the Sages say: it is not a firstborn,
rather, it may be sheared and worked.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, לֹא בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ וְלֹא בַּמְּדִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new case and a three-way מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are not slaughtered. רבי שמעון: this is the greatest blemish. חכמים: an אנדרוגינוס is not a בכור at all and may be sheared and worked.

steps.title: The Torah itself lists גרב and ילפת as blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: how can גרב and חזזית fail to be blemishes, when the Torah lists גרב and ילפת as blemishes?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Is גרב really not a blemish? But the Torah writes "גרב" in its list of blemishes! And is חזזית really not a blemish? But the Torah writes "ילפת"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by pointing out that the משנה seems to contradict a פסוק that lists blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that lists blemishes on a קרבן includes גרב and ילפת. If the Torah calls them blemishes, the משנה should not put them on the list of things that are not blemishes. The link between ילפת and חזזית is proven in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (used to raise a challenge from a פסוק)
A skin disease listed in the Torah's list of blemishes

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And boils are not [a blemish]?
But "garav" is written in the Torah!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:22

phrases.english: And a rash is not [a blemish]?
But "yalefet" is written in the Torah!
phrases.notes: It is in the same פסוק. The next lines show that ילפת is a kind of חזזית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's list in step 7 using a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that גרב and חזזית do not permit slaughtering a בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah explicitly lists גרב and ילפת among the blemishes, so they should count as real blemishes.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that ילפת is the Egyptian חזזית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא identifies the Torah's ילפת as the Egyptian חזזית, and ריש לקיש explains that it is called ילפת because it clings until death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: "גרב" is the hard sore called חרס. "ילפת" is the Egyptian חזזית. And ריש לקיש said: Why is it called "ילפת"? Because it keeps wrapping around the person until the day he dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge. It brings a ברייתא showing that the Torah's ילפת really is a kind of חזזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this ברייתא, someone could say ילפת has nothing to do with חזזית. The ברייתא connects the two, so the contradiction with the משנה is real. ריש לקיש adds that this kind never goes away, which will matter in the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A hard sore, hard like earthenware

phrases.english: And it is taught: "Garav" is the cheres,
phrases.notes: A sore that is hard like earthenware.

phrases.english: "Yalefet" is the Egyptian rash,
And Reish Lakish said:
Why is it called "yalefet"?
Because it keeps clinging until the day of death.
phrases.notes: It's a play on the name: ילפת sounds like מלפפת, "wraps around."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second half of the challenge in step 9 by showing that ילפת is a type of חזזית.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah's ילפת is a form of חזזית, so the משנה contradicts the Torah
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא, along with ריש לקיש's explanation of the name

steps.title: The two kinds of חזזית are different
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction about חזזית is easy to solve: the Torah means the Egyptian kind, and the משנה means the ordinary kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is true that the two mentions of חזזית are not a problem. Here, in the Torah, it means the Egyptian חזזית. There, in the משנה, it means an ordinary חזזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles half of the question. It says the חזזית problem is not hard, and it uses the word "בשלמא" to set up the next point, that the גרב problem still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא itself said the Torah's ילפת is specifically the Egyptian חזזית, which according to ריש לקיש never heals. So the משנה, which says חזזית is not a blemish, must mean the regular kind. The two sources are talking about different illnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable (one part works, but another part is still a problem)
Here... there (two sources speak about different cases)

phrases.english: Granted, rash against rash is not difficult:
here it is about the Egyptian rash,
phrases.notes: This is the Torah's ילפת.

phrases.english: there it is about an ordinary rash.
phrases.notes: This is the חזזית in our משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חזזית half of the challenge in steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different types of חזזית
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Torah's ילפת and the משנה's חזזית are the same thing, so the two sources contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah means the incurable Egyptian חזזית. The משנה means the ordinary kind.

steps.title: The גרב contradiction is still a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the contradiction between the Torah's גרב and the משנה's גרב is still difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the contradiction between גרב and גרב is still a problem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that its first answer only solved חזזית. Nothing has yet explained why the Torah calls גרב a blemish while the משנה says it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ילפת the ברייתא named a special kind, the Egyptian one, so the משנה could mean a different kind. For גרב it only said it is חרס, and that gives no hint that the משנה's גרב is something else. The same word appears in both places with opposite rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: But (here: but this other part is still a problem)

phrases.english: But boils against boils is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the בשלמא structure from step 11 by stating which part is still unanswered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that גרב is not a blemish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah calls the same גרב a blemish, and so far no difference between them has been found.

steps.title: Moist גרב heals, dry גרב does not
steps.stepSummary: The גרב contradiction is also solved: the משנה means moist גרב, which heals, and the Torah means dry גרב, which does not heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גרב contradiction is also not a problem. This one, the משנה, is about moist גרב. That one, the Torah, is about dry גרב. Moist גרב heals. Dry גרב does not heal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the remaining question. There are two kinds of גרב, and only one of them is a real blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish that lets us slaughter a בכור has to be permanent. Moist גרב heals, so it is only temporary, and that is why the משנה says we do not slaughter for it. Dry גרב never heals, so it is the permanent blemish the Torah lists.
steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions are solved the same way. The Torah's blemish is an incurable kind (Egyptian חזזית, dry גרב), while the משנה means a kind that can heal (ordinary חזזית, moist גרב), and a בכור is not slaughtered for a blemish that can heal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the idea behind the whole list in the משנה: a בכור may be slaughtered only for a blemish that will not go away.

phrases.english: Boils against boils is also not difficult,
this is about moist, that is about dry.
phrases.notes: The moist kind is the משנה's גרב. The dry kind is the Torah's גרב.

phrases.english: Moist heals; dry does not heal.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּרָב אַגָּרָב נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּלַח, הָא בְּיָבֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge left standing in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: moist גרב versus dry גרב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Torah's גרב and the משנה's גרב are the same, so the two sources contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means moist גרב, which heals and so is only temporary. The Torah means dry גרב, which never heals.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's חזזית and גרב are the kinds that can heal, so they are not permanent blemishes. The Torah's versions are the incurable kinds.

steps.title: Does moist גרב really heal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 13's claim that moist גרב heals, using a פסוק that calls the Egyptian גרב incurable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does moist גרב really heal? The Torah says, 'The Lord will strike you with the boil of Egypt... and with גרב and with חרס, from which you cannot be healed.' Since חרס is listed separately, the גרב in that פסוק must be the moist kind. Yet the פסוק says it cannot be healed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It quotes a פסוק showing that a moist kind of גרב cannot be healed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said moist גרב heals and only dry גרב does not. But the פסוק in דברים lists both גרב and חרס. חרס is the hard, dry kind, so the גרב next to it must be the moist kind. The פסוק calls both incurable, so it seems moist גרב does not heal either.

keyTerms.meaning: A hard, dry kind of boil (like earthenware)

phrases.english: And does moist [גרב] heal?
But isn't it written: "The Lord will smite you with the boil of Egypt, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 28:27. The rest of the פסוק lists גרב and חרס too.

phrases.english: And since it is written "and with חרס,"
then the גרב mentioned there is moist גרב,
and it says: "from which you cannot be healed"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 13's claim that moist גרב heals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק in דברים lists a moist גרב (next to dry חרס) and calls it incurable.

steps.title: There are three kinds of גרב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there are three kinds of גרב: the Torah's blemish kind, the משנה's kind, and the Egyptian kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there are three kinds of גרב. The kind in the פסוק about blemishes is dry both inside and outside. The kind in the משנה is moist outside and inside. The Egyptian kind is dry inside and moist outside, as it says: 'And it became a boil breaking out in blisters on man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes its answer by splitting גרב into three types instead of two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Egyptian גרב is moist only on the outside, which is why the פסוק in דברים could pair it with חרס. It is still dry inside, so it does not heal. The משנה's גרב is moist all the way through, so it can heal and is not a blemish. The blemish in the Torah is dry all the way through.

keyTerms.meaning: Blisters, which ooze and are moist

steps.whatToRemember: There are three kinds of גרב. The blemish kind is dry inside and out. The משנה's kind is moist inside and out, so it heals. The Egyptian kind is dry inside and moist outside, so it does not heal.

phrases.english: Rather, there are three [kinds]:

phrases.aramaic: דִּקְרָא — יָבֵשׁ בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: the one of the verse is dry both on the inside and on the outside;
the one of the משנה is moist on the outside and the inside;
the one of Egypt is dry on the inside and moist on the outside,
as it is written: "And it became a boil breaking forth with blisters upon man."
phrases.notes: שמות 9:10. Blisters ooze, which shows the Egyptian kind is moist on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits one category into three distinct types
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any גרב moist on the outside would heal, but the פסוק calls the Egyptian moist גרב incurable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only גרב that is moist inside and out (the משנה's kind) heals. The Egyptian kind is dry inside and does not heal.

steps.title: Where do we learn the rule about old, sick, and foul-smelling animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה and asks for their source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'An old animal, a sick animal, and a foul-smelling animal.' Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה and asks where its rule comes from. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says these animals cannot be brought as קרבנות, even though they are not full blemishes. The גמרא wants a Torah source for that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we learn these things?

phrases.english: "And the old, the sick, and the foul-smelling."
From where are these matters [derived]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next words of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for disqualifying old, sick, and foul-smelling animals

steps.title: The three times מן appear in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns the three exclusions from the three times the word מן appears in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: 'From the flock, from the sheep, and from the goats.' This comes to exclude the old, the sick, and the foul-smelling animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The source is a פסוק about קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מן means 'from', which suggests 'some of them, not all.' It appears three times, so each one excludes one type of animal: old, sick, and foul-smelling.

keyTerms.meaning: From, meaning some and not all

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"From the flock, and from the sheep, and from the goats"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:10. The word "from" appears three times, and each one excludes something.

phrases.english: to exclude the old, the sick, and the foul-smelling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three times מן appears in ויקרא 1:10 exclude the old, the sick, and the foul-smelling animal.

steps.title: Why the Torah had to exclude both old and sick animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that excluding an old animal and a sick animal are both needed, because neither could be learned from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the Torah had only excluded an old animal, I would say that is because it will never get healthy again. But a sick animal can get better, so I would say it is allowed. And if the Torah had only excluded a sick animal, I would say that is because being sick is not normal. But growing old is normal, so I would say an old animal is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the Torah needed separate exclusions for an old animal and a sick animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has a reason that might make it different from the other. An old animal never recovers, while a sick one might. Sickness is unusual, while old age is natural. So we could not learn one case from the other, and the Torah had to teach both.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed, none is extra

steps.whatToRemember: An old animal and a sick animal each needed their own exclusion. Old age never goes away but is natural. Sickness can go away but is not natural.

phrases.english: And [both] are necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written [only] to exclude an old one,
[I would say that is] because it does not become healthy again,
but a sick one, which does become healthy again,
I would say [it is] not [excluded].
And if it had written [only] to exclude a sick one,
[I would say that is] because that is not its normal way,
but an old one, for that is its normal way,
I would say [it is] not [excluded].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the exclusions listed in Step 17 are each needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exclusions of an old animal and a sick animal are both needed, because each has a reason that could have made it allowed.

steps.title: Why All Three Exclusions Are Needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא. Two exclusions alone would not have covered the foul-smelling animal, and one exclusion for the foul-smelling animal would not have covered the old and sick ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written only two exclusions, I would have said they exclude the weak animals, the old and the sick. A foul-smelling animal is not weak, so I would have said it is allowed. If the Torah had only excluded the foul-smelling animal, I would have said that is because it is disgusting. The old and sick animals are not disgusting, so I would have said they are allowed. So all three are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes showing that each of the three exclusions teaches something the others could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old and sick animals share one problem: they are weak. The foul-smelling animal has a different problem: it is disgusting. Because the reasons are different, you cannot learn one group from the other, so the Torah had to spell out all three.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, a name for ה׳ as Author of the Torah
Foul-smelling (the animal with a bad odor)
They are necessary, so each one is needed

steps.whatToRemember: Old and sick animals are disqualified because they are weak. A foul-smelling animal is disqualified because it is disgusting. Since the reasons differ, the Torah needed all three exclusions.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written two,
phrases.notes: Two of the three exclusions from the word מן.

phrases.english: [I would say they are] to exclude these that are weak,
but a foul-smelling one, which is not weak,
I would say not [excluded],
and alternatively, [if it had been written only] to exclude the foul-smelling one
because it is repulsive,
but these, which are not repulsive,
I would say not [excluded]; so they are all necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends Step 18's צריכותא between old and sick to include the third exclusion, the foul-smelling animal, and closes the discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the three exclusions is needed, because weakness and repulsiveness are separate reasons for disqualifying an animal.

steps.title: Source for an Animal Used in a Sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, about an animal used for a sin, and asks where this rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And an animal with which a sin was done, etc.' Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next words of the משנה and asks for their source. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה disqualifies animals connected to a sin, such as one used for bestiality or one that killed a person. The גמרא wants to find where the Torah teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words learned? (a request for the source)

phrases.english: And one with which a transgression was performed, etc.
From where are these matters [derived]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה, the same way Step 16 opened the previous topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for disqualifying an animal involved in a sin.

steps.title: Four Exclusions From the Words of the Verse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads each 'from' in the פסוק as an exclusion. This gives four disqualified animals: one involved in bestiality, one worshipped as a god, one set aside for idol worship, and one that gored and killed a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: 'From the animal' excludes an animal that lay with a person or that a person lay with. 'From the herd' excludes an animal that was worshipped. 'From the flock' excludes an animal set aside for idol worship. 'And from the flock' excludes an animal that gored and killed a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that learns each disqualified animal from a different word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'from' (מן) narrows down which animals may be brought, so each one removes a type of animal. The extra 'and' (ו) in 'and from the flock' adds one more exclusion, the animal that killed a person.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that lay with a person
An animal that a person lay with (bestiality)
An animal that was itself worshipped as a god
Here: an animal set aside to be used for idol worship
An animal that gored and killed a person

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"From the cattle" comes to exclude an animal that lay with a person or that was lain with,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:2

phrases.english: "from the herd" comes to exclude one that was worshipped,
"from the flock" comes to exclude one set aside [for idol worship],
"and from the flock" comes to exclude one that gored [and killed a person].
phrases.notes: The extra letter ו, 'and', counts as one more exclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20's request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each 'from' in ויקרא 1:2, plus the extra 'and', excludes one kind of animal: רובע and נרבע, נעבד, מוקצה, and נוגח.

steps.title: These Animals Are Killed Anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a רובע, a נרבע and a נוגח are put to death by בית דין, so it seems no פסוק is needed to keep them off the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these animals are sentenced to death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. These animals are stoned anyway, so why would the Torah need to exclude them from being a קרבן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal sentenced to death cannot be brought as a קרבן, so the exclusion seems pointless. The challenge suggests there must be a case where the animal is not killed.

keyTerms.meaning: Ones who are sentenced to death

phrases.english: These are liable to be killed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the need for some of the exclusions in Step 21's ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's exclusions for רובע, נרבע and נוגח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These animals are executed by בית דין anyway, so a פסוק excluding them from the מזבח seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Only One Witness or the Owner Knows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is one where only one witness or the owner says it happened. That is not enough to put the animal to death, but it is enough to disqualify it as a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where it is known through one witness, or through the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing a case where the animal is not put to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting an animal to death requires two witnesses, so with only one witness or the owner the animal stays alive. The פסוק teaches that even then, the animal may not be brought as a קרבן.
steps.whatToRemember: An animal connected to a sin is disqualified from the מזבח even when the evidence is too weak to have it put to death, such as one witness or the owner's own word.
steps.whyThisMatters: This also explains the משנה's wording, which mentions one witness or the owner. That is exactly the case where the פסוק is needed.

phrases.english: [It is a case known] through one witness
phrases.notes: Putting an animal to death needs two witnesses, so here it stays alive.

phrases.english: or through the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד אוֹ עַל פִּי הַבְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to evidence too weak for execution
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These animals are always executed, so excluding them from the מזבח is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: With only one witness or the owner, the animal is not executed, but it is still disqualified as a קרבן.

steps.title: Why a טומטום cannot be slaughtered anywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that a טומטום cannot be slaughtered in the מקדש, because it may be female, and cannot be slaughtered in the country, because it may be an unblemished male בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, a טומטום is not slaughtered in the מקדש, because maybe it is a female. And it is not slaughtered in the country, because maybe it is a male with no מום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the easy half of the משנה's rule, the טומטום. This is a setup: it gets the easy case out of the way so the גמרא can ask about the harder case next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טומטום has its sex organs covered, so we do not know if it is male or female. If it is female, it is not a בכור and cannot be brought as a קרבן in the מקדש. If it is male, it is a holy בכור with no מום, so it cannot be slaughtered as ordinary meat in the country.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose sex organs are covered, so we cannot tell if it is male or female
'Granted' or 'it makes sense'. It opens the easy case before the גמרא asks about a harder one
The Temple, where a בכור is brought as a קרבן
'The country', meaning outside the מקדש, where a blemished בכור may be slaughtered and eaten
A blemish. It makes a בכור unfit for the מזבח and lets it be eaten as ordinary meat

phrases.english: Granted, a tumtum:
not in the Temple, because perhaps it is a female;
not in the country,

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא זָכָר הוּא וְלֵית בֵּהּ מוּמָא.
phrases.english: because perhaps it is a male and it has no blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the animals disqualified for a sin to the משנה's rule about a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום is slaughtered neither in the מקדש (maybe female) nor in the country (maybe an unblemished male).

steps.title: Why can't an אנדרוגינוס be slaughtered in the country?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: an אנדרוגינוס may be female, so it cannot go to the מקדש. But even if it is male, its female organ should count as a 'crack', which is a מום, so it should be allowed to be slaughtered in the country.
steps.simpleTranslation: But an אנדרוגינוס: granted it is not slaughtered in the מקדש, because maybe it is female. But why not in the country too? Even if it is male, let its female organ count as a crack, and let it be slaughtered because of that מום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule for the אנדרוגינוס. It says the female organ should count as a crack, which is a מום, so the animal should be allowed in the country.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אנדרוגינוס has both male and female organs. If it is female, it is not a בכור at all. If it is male, the female organ looks like a crack in the body, and the Torah lists 'cracked' (חרוץ) as a מום. Either way it would seem fine to slaughter it outside the מקדש, so why does the משנה forbid it?

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that has both male and female sex organs
A crack or slit. Here the גמרא suggests it counts as the מום of 'cracked'
'Even granting that'. It concedes a point for the sake of argument

phrases.english: But a hermaphrodite:
granted, not in the Temple,
because perhaps it is a female.
But in the country also, why not?
Even granting that it is a male,
let its female organ be considered a crack,
and let one slaughter it on account of that!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the harder case with the טומטום case granted in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that an אנדרוגינוס may not be slaughtered in the country.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if it is male, its female organ should count as the מום of חרוץ, which would allow it to be slaughtered outside the מקדש.

steps.title: אביי: 'cracked' must be in a bone, like 'broken'
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the פסוק puts חרוץ next to שבור. Just as a break happens in a bone, the crack that counts as a מום must also be in a bone. The female organ is not in a bone, so it is not a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says 'or cracked or broken'. 'Cracked' is like 'broken'. Just as 'broken' is where there is a bone, so too 'cracked' is where there is a bone.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. He reads the פסוק so that 'cracked' only counts as a מום when it is in a bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists חרוץ and שבור together, so אביי learns one from the other. You can only 'break' a bone, not soft flesh. So the crack that counts as a מום must also be in a bone, and the female organ, which is in flesh, does not qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Cracked', a מום listed in the Torah
'Broken', a מום listed right next to חָרוּץ
'Similar to'. One word in the פסוק is learned from the word next to it
'The place of a bone', a part of the body where there is bone

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The verse states: "Or cracked or broken."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:22

phrases.english: Cracked is similar to broken:
just as broken is in the place of a bone,
so too cracked is in the place of a bone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אָמַר קְרָא ״אוֹ חָרוּץ אוֹ שָׁבוּר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the definition of the מום through a reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any crack, even in flesh such as the female organ, counts as the מום of חרוץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a crack in a bone counts as חרוץ, so the female organ of an אנדרוגינוס is not a מום.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why an אנדרוגינוס בכור stays forbidden in the country: its female organ does not count as a מום.

steps.title: רבא: even without 'broken', a crack in flesh is not a מום
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even without comparing to שבור, a crack in flesh cannot be a מום. He starts to prove it: the ברייתא calls גרב hard boils like pottery, and such a sore counts as a crack, since the Torah describes a skin sore as looking 'deeper than the skin'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even without 'broken', you cannot say that a crack where there is only flesh is a מום. Because if you thought it was a מום, look at this: the ברייתא said that 'גרב' means sores hard as pottery. That is a kind of crack, as it is written, 'and its appearance is deeper than the skin', like sunlight that looks deeper than the shade.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same challenge. He begins a proof from the מום called גרב that a crack in flesh cannot be its own מום. The next step finishes his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא points out that a hard skin sore (גרב) already counts as a crack in the flesh, because the Torah describes skin sores as looking sunken. He is setting up this point: if every crack in flesh were the מום of חרוץ, the Torah would not need to list גרב separately. So 'cracked' must mean something else, not a crack in flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: A skin disease listed in the Torah as a מום
Pottery. Here it describes sores that are as hard as earthenware
'The place of flesh', a part of the body with no bone
'If it would enter your mind', an opening for a line of thought the גמרא is about to reject

steps.confusionAlert: רבא agrees with אביי's conclusion: a crack in flesh is not a מום. He only disagrees about the source. אביי needs the comparison to שבור; רבא proves it even without that comparison.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even without the comparison to "broken,"
you cannot say
that a crack in the place of flesh is a blemish.
For if it would enter your mind that it is a blemish,
then since the ברייתא said "garav" is sores hard as pottery,
that is a crack,
as it is written: "And its appearance is deeper than the skin,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:30

phrases.english: like the appearance of sunlight, which looks deeper than the shade.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בְּלָא שָׁבוּר נָמֵי לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the קשיא of Step 25, one that does not rely on אביי's comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proves from how the list of מומין is built that a crack in flesh is not חרוץ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the comparison to שבור, one might think a crack in flesh counts as חרוץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since גרב is already a crack in flesh and is listed on its own, חרוץ cannot mean a crack in flesh. Step 28 finishes the proof.

steps.title: Why the Torah needed to write גרב
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his proof. If a crack in flesh were a מום, the תורה would not need to list גרב, since גרב is even worse. So writing גרב teaches that a crack in flesh is not a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a crack in flesh were a מום, the תורה could have written only 'cracked' and skipped 'גרב'. We would have figured it out ourselves: if a crack, which is not disgusting, is a מום, then גרב, which is disgusting, surely is. Since the תורה still wrote 'גרב', it is teaching us that a crack in a place of flesh is not a מום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the proof רבא began in the last step. It shows that the extra word גרב in the פסוק only makes sense if a crack in flesh does not count as a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27 רבא said that גרב is a kind of crack that sits in the flesh. If every crack, even in flesh, were a מום, then listing גרב would be pointless, because a disgusting crack would follow by כל שכן from a plain crack. Since the תורה does not waste words, writing גרב shows that a crack in flesh is not a מום on its own. So the female organ of an אנדרוגינוס, which is in flesh, is not a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳ who wrote it
All the more so, a reasoning from a lighter case to a stronger one
In a place of flesh, where there is no bone

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the extra word גרב in the פסוק teaches that a crack in flesh alone is not a מום, so the אנדרוגינוס's female organ is not a מום.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say that גרב is not a מום. גרב is a מום because the תורה wrote it. His point is that a plain crack in flesh, without that special word, would not count.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a second, separate reason why an אנדרוגינוס cannot be slaughtered in the country as a blemished בכור. It does not depend on אביי's comparison to שבור.

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write only "cracked"
and not need to write "garav",
and I would say: if "cracked," which is not repulsive,
is a blemish,
then "garav," which is repulsive, is it not all the more so a blemish?
The Merciful One wrote "garav"
to say that a crack in a place of flesh
is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's alternative answer to step 25, begun in step 27, using the extra word גרב in the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that a crack in flesh is not a מום
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word גרב in the list of מומים (ויקרא 22:22), which would be unneeded if a crack in flesh were already a מום

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל calls it the greatest blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי ישמעאל from the משנה, who says there is no bigger מום than the condition of an אנדרוגינוס. This seems to go against both אביי and רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: there is no blemish greater than this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opinion of רבי ישמעאל from the משנה. This sets up the next steps, which explain why he does not agree with אביי or רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that the female organ of an אנדרוגינוס is a real מום, so the animal may be slaughtered in the country. That is the very idea the גמרא raised in step 25, which אביי and רבא rejected. So the גמרא now has to explain how רבי ישמעאל understands the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: You have no, there is no

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה about the אנדרוגינוס. In the משנה above, the same line is said by רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: You have no blemish greater than this.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: אֵין לְךָ מוּם גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a תנא who holds the very view that אביי and רבא just rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, the female organ of an אנדרוגינוס is a great מום, so it may be slaughtered as a blemished בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answers of אביי (step 26) and רבא (steps 27–28) that a crack in flesh, like the female organ of an אנדרוגינוס, is not a מום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא calls the אנדרוגינוס's condition the greatest מום, so he must count a crack in flesh as a מום. That seems to go against both proofs.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל does not compare crack to break
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל does not hold like אביי. He does not compare חרוץ to שבור, so for him a crack does not have to be in a bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not hold like אביי. We do not say that 'cracked' is like 'broken'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first reason רבי ישמעאל can call the female organ a מום: he rejects אביי's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי learned from the closeness of חרוץ and שבור in the פסוק that a crack must be in a bone, like a break. רבי ישמעאל does not learn that comparison. So for him a crack in flesh can also count as a מום.

phrases.english: He does not hold like Abaye,
phrases.notes: He means רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: that "cracked" is similar to "broken"
we do not say.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּאַבָּיֵי לָא אָמַר, חָרוּץ דּוּמְיָא דְּשָׁבוּר לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי ישמעאל avoids אביי's reasoning from step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting a comparison drawn from the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since אביי compared חרוץ to שבור, it seemed a crack must be in a bone, so רבי ישמעאל's view looked hard to explain.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל does not learn that comparison, so a crack in flesh can be a מום for him.

steps.title: A visible crack in flesh is an ill blemish
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל also does not hold like רבא. Maybe רבא's rule only covers a crack in flesh that is hard to see. A crack that is easy to see, like this one, is called a 'מום רע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also does not hold like רבא. Perhaps the rule that a crack in flesh is not a מום is only where it cannot be noticed. But where it can be noticed, we call it an 'ill blemish'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second reason רבי ישמעאל can call the female organ a מום: he limits רבא's proof to cracks that are hard to see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא proved from the word גרב that a crack in flesh is not a מום. רבי ישמעאל could say that proof only covers a crack nobody notices. A crack that is easy to see, like the female organ of an אנדרוגינוס, fits the words 'מום רע' in the פסוק, so it is a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: An ill blemish, a phrase from the פסוק
I read it into this case, the words apply here

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל disagrees with both answers. He does not compare חרוץ to שבור like אביי, and he limits רבא's rule to cracks that are not visible. A visible crack in flesh is a 'מום רע', so the אנדרוגינוס has a מום.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one משנה opinion can stand against two separate proofs, each in its own way.

phrases.english: He also does not hold like Rava,
since perhaps that rule is only where it is not noticeable,
phrases.notes: He means רבא's rule from the extra word גרב, that a crack in flesh is not a מום.

phrases.english: but where it is noticeable,
I call it "an ill blemish."
phrases.notes: דברים 15:21

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרָבָא נָמֵי לָא אָמַר, דִּילְמָא הֵיכָא דְּלָא מִינַּכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reason for רבי ישמעאל's view, this time against רבא's proof from steps 27 and 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the other rule to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's proof from גרב seemed to show that no crack in flesh is ever a מום.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל can limit that proof to cracks that are not visible. A visible one is a 'מום רע'.
